fields.meta_description: Build a shipping address form that gets a label-ready address from every recipient and reminds anyone who has not replied. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Shipping Address Form That Fills Every Label
fields.hero_description: Create a shipping address form with fields in label order, reply reminders, and a lock date, all saved to a table you own.
fields.features_heading: Fields a Mailing List Can Ship From
fields.features_subheading: Addresses pasted in from email threads are where packages go missing. These six pieces fix each one before it reaches a label.
fields.feature_1:
Fields in the order a label reads

Ask for the name first, the street and unit next and the city line last, the order USPS reads a delivery address. Each column of the export lines up with a label template.
fields.feature_2:
A unit line nobody skips

Ask whether the address has an apartment or suite, and require the number when the answer is yes. It prints at the end of the street line, where USPS prefers it to sit.
fields.feature_3:
Address fields that follow the country

Show US fields by default and swap in region and postal code fields once someone picks another country. The country name prints alone on the last line, in capitals, as USPS asks.
fields.feature_4:
Reminders for anyone who has not replied

Email each recipient a personal link, then remind anyone still missing after the number of days you choose. The addresses table shows at a glance who has replied and who has not.
fields.feature_5:
A lock date before the export

Let recipients correct their own address until a date you set, then freeze the list. Late edits wait for a named approver to clear them instead of slipping into the export.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take with you

Export the full codebase to your GitHub on paid plans when the form has to live inside your store or fulfillment stack. The form and its addresses table come along with the code.

fields.tab_content_1:
Hoodie sizes ride along with each home address

Fernway's people team ships a hoodie to its 140 remote employees each year. Each person gets a link that asks for a size and a home address, unit line included. Anyone who has not answered after 3 days gets one email reminder. By Thursday, 128 of 140 have replied. The other 12 got their reminder that morning.
fields.tab_content_2:
Winners in Canada see province and postal code

The Low Tide podcast picks 25 listeners to win a signed record. Its claim form shows state and ZIP Code for US winners and swaps in province and postal code when a winner picks Canada. Each winner has 7 days to claim. A winner in Halifax enters B3H 4R2, and the label prints CANADA on the last line.
fields.tab_content_3:
No backer edits after lock day

Tidewater Games funded its second board game with 1,200 backers and needs an address for every copy. Backers confirm or fix their own address until lock day, 9 days before the export to the fulfillment warehouse. So far 1,134 have confirmed. A change after the lock goes to Priya on the support team.
fields.tab_content_4:
Any PO box bounces back for a street address

Every December, account managers at Halden Pike add clients to the agency's holiday gift list, 60 boxes this year. The gift courier only delivers to street addresses. An entry with a PO box goes back to the account manager who added it, with a note asking for the client's office address.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Shipping Address Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a shipping address form that returns a correct address for every package, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List who you are shipping to
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Put the fields in label order
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Decide which countries you ship to
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Add what travels with the address
fields.howto_step_1_des: Gather the people you are shipping to and how to reach them, such as a staff directory or a backer export. Each person gets a personal link, and every reply matches back to the right row.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Order the fields the way the label prints them, top to bottom, with the unit on the street line. People filling the form in then see their address the way the carrier will read it.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Settle the list of countries before anyone fills the form in. Each country you add gets its own region and postal code fields, and a country outside the list gets a short note saying you cannot ship there.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Add the questions that belong next to the address, such as a hoodie size or a delivery note about a gate code. Keep it short, since each extra field is one more reason a recipient closes the tab.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write one prompt with the fields and the countries, plus the reminder schedule and lock date. Emergent builds the shipping address form and the addresses table behind it. Change anything later by asking, such as moving the lock date.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Set reminders and a lock date
fields.howto_step_6_des: Pick how many days pass before a reminder goes out and the date the list freezes. After that date, edits need a person's approval, since the old address may already be printed on a label.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill the form in yourself with an awkward address, like a fourth-floor suite or a Canadian postal code. Check that the export lines up with your label template before the link goes out to anyone else.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is mostly address-format guides (PostGrid, a USPS FAQ, an address-validation blog), a CodePen snippet, a Formbold template, a Bowdoin mailroom PDF and a NetSuite thread on relabeling a field. None of them deals with the real job behind a shipping address form: getting a correct, label-ready address back from dozens or hundreds of people who are not in the room. This page shows that job for four senders (a remote team getting swag, giveaway winners, crowdfunding backers, a client gift list), with fields in the order a USPS label reads, a unit line that cannot be skipped, reminders for people who have not answered, a lock before export, and PO box checks for couriers. It answers the PAA questions on writing, entering and naming a shipping address plainly. Internal shipping requests stay on the shipping form sibling; buying and paying stay on order form and payment form.

findings.quote: copy: 'Backers confirm or fix their own address until lock day, 9 days before the export to the fulfillment warehouse. ... A change after the lock goes to Priya on the support team.' / image: 'Lock day | In 9 days', 'Warehouse export | After the lock', hero 'Edit after lock goes to Priya ... now'; alt 'with lock day in 9 days, and an address change requested after the lock waits for Priya'
findings.issue: The copy's 9 days is the gap between lock and export; the image makes it the time until the lock, and then shows a post-lock edit arriving now, before the lock has happened. The story link pairs 'until lock day, 9 days before the export' with 'In 9 days', which mean different things. Only tab with this defect.
findings.fix: Draw the timeline as lock day then export '9 days later' (or set today after the lock, e.g. 'Locked 2 days ago', 'Export in 7 days'), so a post-lock edit can exist; update the story pair and alt to match.

findings.quote: image: hero card channel 'support' ('# support') titled 'Edit after lock goes to Priya' / copy: 'A change after the lock goes to Priya on the support team.'
findings.issue: The copy routes the change to one named person; the image posts it to a shared channel. Only instance: tabs 1, 2 and 4 draw no channel.
findings.fix: Draw the hero as a card or email to Priya (e.g. 'To Priya, support'), not a channel post.

findings.quote: No single format covers every country, since each one orders its lines and postal codes differently. Follow the destination country's order for everything above the last line.
findings.issue: A statement of fact about international postal formats with no supporting spec.domain_sources entry; the cited USPS IMM 122 page says the city and post code go in capitals, the last line shows only the country name, and at most five lines, but not that each country orders its lines differently or that the destination's order applies. Only instance of this class on the page.
findings.fix: Add a source that states it (UPU or USPS guidance on writing the address in the destination country's format), or cut to the sourced points: city and post code in capitals, country name alone on the last line.
